# Interpretation — issue #1417, analyzer first pass (round 1)

**Bottom line.** The run's per-lane headlines do not survive verification. The verdict layer of the identity battery — REL = composed-transport R² divided by a within-reference ceiling refit on judge-kept row subsets — is voided by a known, documented failure mode of the frozen #825 ridge instrument: the generalized-cross-validation (GCV) lambda selection collapses to the grid-minimum on many judge-filtered row subsets, driving held-out R² to −0.6…−1.5 on row sets whose supersets (all 4,724 rows) and random subsets (matched n=516) fit healthily at +0.3…+0.65. Ten of twelve within-reference ceilings in the context-arm battery pairs against the chat/plain-text references are negative (broken; the two positive ones, +0.077 and +0.306, sit far below their 0.654/0.542 full-n anchors — the collapse is graded, not binary), so every "Distinct" verdict — including both cells feeding the base-model lane's "user-directed-only" table lookup — is a denominator artifact. The instruct lane's "unresolved — content confound" conclusion happens to stand, but for reasons partly different from the ones the dispatcher recorded. The experiment's Goal question (helpful register vs speaking-to-a-user) is **unanswered by this run**; the decisive follow-up is a re-fit with the instrument's own registered mitigations engaged (`fit825.GCV_DOF_CAP = 0.9` and/or `lambda_selection="inner-group-cv"` — both documented in `scripts/issue825_fit_cells.py` lines 68–91 and neither engaged by `scripts/issue1417_battery.py`).

## Findings

**1. (Headline, methodological) The frozen ridge instrument's GCV lambda selection collapses on judge-filtered row subsets, voiding the run's map-identity verdict layer.** Three of five instruct cell maps read "no map" (R² −0.6…−1.5) solely because of this; 10 of 12 within-reference ceilings against C0/C0′ are negative. Every "Distinct" verdict in `battery_summary.json` divides a healthy positive numerator by a broken negative ceiling; every instruct "Shared" verdict divides two broken negatives. The four-line evidence chain (matched-subsample recovery, random-projection control, overshoot cosine signature, the instrument's own #1335 documentation with un-engaged mitigations) makes this HIGH confidence.

**2. Both lane headlines in `epm:results` are unsupported.** The pretrained "H2 (user-directed-only)" lookup is void twice over: its exposition-Distinct input is a broken-denominator artifact (numerator +0.409/+0.436 ≈ 75% of the full-n anchors — if anything Shared-leaning), and its rude-Shared input comes from an exploratory cell (10.9% yield, content-collapsed, own-map R² −0.002 — "map existence" cleared only the very wide n=516 null band, a gate mis-calibration at small n). The instruct "unresolved — content confound" outcome stands, but its per-cell verdicts are equally void; the valid part is the manipulation-check failure, not the REL lattice.

**3. (Valid, data-level) The register-vs-content decoupling failed at the manipulation-check layer in both lanes.** The one cell designed to discriminate helpful register from user-directedness (rude-but-informative) collapsed answer content on the instruct model (variance ratio 0.486 < 0.5, borderline) and under-yielded catastrophically on the base model (10.9%). Even with a healthy instrument, this run could not have delivered the helpful-register half of the verdict table. The base model largely cannot sustain rude-but-informative register under a system prompt (expected — base models weakly follow system prompts), and the instruct model trades content variance for rudeness.

**4. (Valid, positive) The single fully-healthy battery pair reads Shared: base model, non-user-addressee vs helpful-instruction reference (n=1588).** Every component is healthy and concordant: ceilings 0.384/0.388; REL 0.937 (bootstrap CI 0.928–0.946, fixed-maps-resampled-rows convention), reverse direction 0.959; stable across layers 14/18 (0.92/0.94); raw map cosine 0.523, rotation-aligned 0.634 (chance band p97.5 0.0005, z ≈ 2400, 100 draws); bidirectional FROZEN-map transfer positive (+0.346/+0.339 vs shuffle nulls −0.32/−0.44). Within the base model, swapping the interlocutor from a human user to a named AI relay leaves the context→answer map intact. Scope caveats: single pair; the rubric never verified the model registered the AI-relay framing (plan rule 7 — "ignored instruction OR genuine invariance"); base lane only.

**5. (Descriptive, not verdict-grade) Composed-transport numerators are positive and substantial wherever the cell's own map is healthy — leaning against any strong "distinct map" claim for ANY framing cell.** Against the G1-verified full-n anchors (0.654/0.625 instruct chat/plain, 0.542/0.578 pretrained): instruct rude 0.534 (≈82% of anchor), instruct exposition 0.375/0.330 (≈57%/53%), pretrained helpful-ctrl 0.499 (92%), evasive 0.371 (68%), exposition 0.409/0.436 (≈75%), AI-addressee 0.531 (98%). This normalization is not fold- or row-matched (kept-row selection moved pretrained own-fits UP, e.g. 0.378 kept vs 0.281 all for c1, so the honest ceiling can sit on either side of the anchor) — descriptive only. If it survives the repaired-ceiling refit, the verdict pair would land in the plan's "Neither (generic QA structure)" row — the map as a generic query-answering structure rather than a helpful-register or user-directedness property — but that is a hypothesis for the follow-up, not a finding of this run.

**6. Prefix-arm control behaved as registered** (near-zero own-map R², 0.01–0.13, all 10 cells): within a single-turn fixed-system-prompt cell the prefix is ~constant, so prefix-arm fits are constant-input regressions. No prefix-arm read carries identity evidence (plan rule 6). Notably the prefix fits did NOT trigger the GCV collapse — consistent with GCV correctly selecting heavy regularization when the input carries no signal.

## Goal verdict

**Inconclusive — no valid verdict on whether the shared context→answer map is tied to helpful register or to speaking-to-a-user.** Both the instrument layer (finding 1) and the discriminating cell's data (finding 3) failed. The surviving evidence (findings 4–5) leans toward map invariance across framings — including the addressee manipulations — but cannot be graded against the 0.5 REL boundary until the ceilings are refit with the registered mitigations.

## Proposed title / confidence

"Ridge-regularization collapse on judge-filtered row subsets voids the framing-cell map-identity verdicts; the run's user-directedness headline is a denominator artifact (HIGH confidence)" — confidence attaches to the instrument-failure claim (mechanistically pinned + 4-way corroborated); the Goal question itself is explicitly unresolved, and finding-5's invariance lean is LOW confidence pending the repaired refit.

## Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

The headline overturn (verdict-layer void) is REAL and well-supported — I independently reproduced every number in the fact sheet's two tables from `eval_results/issue_1417/{cells,battery}/` (all 10 cell rows, all 18 pair rows, G1 anchors at abs dev ≤ 1e-16, yields, variance ratios, judge config N=3/max_tokens=300/keep≥50/transport=0, alignment spot values −0.848/−0.738, h_table verdicts). The matched-n recovery is in the JSONs (instruct c1 kept −1.481 vs 5 seeded n=516 subsets of the SAME kept rows at +0.34..+0.38), the #1335 documentation is verbatim at `scripts/issue825_fit_cells.py` lines 68–91, `run_cell` (line 991) does not even expose `lambda_selection` and `issue1417_battery.py` never sets `fit825.GCV_DOF_CAP`, and every broken fit sits at 0.8·n < 3584 while the never-broken full-n fits sit above. The REVISE is for three substantive framing/evidence defects, not the overturn itself.

### Overclaims
- **Evidence line (ii) mischaracterizes the random-projection control** ("a random-input fit cannot legitimately read below its shuffle null (−0.02), so the fitter itself is broken"). The implementation (`issue825_fit_cells.py::random_projection_control`, lines 713–755) replaces X with X @ P where P is a SQUARE d×d Gaussian — the docstring says "same output dimension but scrambled feature axes". That is an information-PRESERVING transform, not a signal-destroying random-input control, and the data confirm it: the control tracks the observed R² almost exactly in EVERY cell (instruct c2 kept obs +0.546 vs rp +0.54; c1 all-rows obs +0.650 vs rp +0.646; identical pattern in all 30 ctx fit JSONs). A genuine random-input fit could not read +0.65. So the control's −2.89 on c1-kept is largely the SAME collapse replicated under a near-rotation of the same input — it shows the failure is not tied to specific feature axes, which is far weaker than the "independent line" the text claims. Weakening: re-describe it as "an information-preserving axis-scramble of the same input reproduces the collapse (−2.89 kept vs +0.646 all-rows), so the failure is a property of the (rows, spectrum) configuration, not of particular feature axes" — or drop it and rest the HIGH claim on the three genuinely independent lines (matched-n recovery, overshoot cosine, documented #1335 mechanism + regime boundary), which still carry it.
- **Finding 4: "Every component is healthy and concordant" is false at L26 of the SAME pair.** `battery_pretrained__c5_ai_addressee__vs_c1__ctx.json` `rel_by_layer["26"]`: ceiling −0.0166, REL −18.18; transfer ref-on-cell L26 −0.094. The pair is healthy at 14/18/19 only — and at n=1588 (0.8·n = 1270 < 3584) it sits INSIDE the vulnerable regime the headline defines, so by the interpretation's own account its L19 ceiling (0.384) could itself be attenuated (graded collapse INFLATES REL). Soften to the enumerated components, name the broken L26 read, and state that the "leans Shared" weight rests on the ceiling-independent map-level reads (cosines 0.523/0.634 vs chance ~0.0005; frozen bidirectional transfers +0.34/+0.35 vs nulls −0.34/−0.45), not on REL alone.
- Precision: "broken fits keep prediction cosine ≈ 0.74" — actual broken-fit L19 cosines are 0.740 (c1), 0.758 (c5), **0.850 (c3)**; healthy 0.950–0.952. The direction holds; state the range (0.74–0.85 vs 0.95), not a single 0.74.

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns
- **The random-projection control ≈ observed R² in every single cell** (healthy and broken alike, to 2 decimals) — nowhere mentioned, and it is what reveals the control is information-preserving (see above). A reader of the fact sheet's line (ii) alone would infer the opposite.
- **L26 ceiling broken (−0.017, REL −18.2) inside the one "fully-healthy" pair** — omitted from finding 4 (details above).

## Interpretation — task #1417, follow-up round `registered-selector-refit`

### Raw-output spot check (5 random rows)

Seed-42 sample of 5 files from the round's 188 refit artifacts (`refit/cells/` + `refit/battery/`); this round generates no new completions, so the raw outputs are fit/battery JSONs:

1. `battery_instruct__c2_rude__vs_c1__prefix.json` — prefix-arm battery, n = 2,725; rel 0.578, CI 0.558–0.599. Not fishy: prefix arm is the designed degenerate control (own-map R² ≤ 0.13); carries no identity evidence, as planned.
2. `cells_c2_rude__pretrained__ctx__matched2.json` — matched-n companion, n_allow = 516, r2_l19 0.1439, selector `inner-group-cv`. Not fishy: for the base rude cell the matched-n draw IS the full kept set (n = 516), so it must equal the kept fit — it does.
3. `cells_c1_helpful_ctrl__instruct__ctx__matched4.json` — n = 516 subsample, r2_l19 0.5396. Not fishy: consistent with run-1 matched-n range for this cell (+0.34…+0.38 under pure GCV; the inner-CV value sits above, as expected when the selector stops interpolating).
4. `cells_c5_ai_addressee__instruct__ctx__matched4.json` — n = 516, r2_l19 0.5149. Not fishy: same pattern as (3).
5. `cells_c4_exposition__pretrained__ctx__matched4.json` — n = 516, r2_l19 0.2922. Not fishy: below the full-n kept fit (0.356), the expected small-n attenuation.

0 of 5 fishy. Every checked file carries `lambda_selection: inner-group-cv` and finite selected λs.

### Finding

With the plan's `inner-group-cv` λ-selection fallback wired into the battery (the single change; same stores, judge-kept row allowlists, folds, λ grid, layers, pairs, and draw counts as run 1), **all 10 (framing cell × model) fits return a map (`map_exists: true`) and all 10 vs-chat-reference pairs read Shared**: recovery fractions 0.71–1.00 with 95% bootstrap CIs wholly above the 0.5 verdict boundary, rotation-aligned map cosines 0.37–0.77 against a random-rotation chance band near 0.0005, composition nulls near −0.02 to −0.08 vs observed numerators +0.30 to +0.67. The (rude, exposition) verdict-pair lookup lands on "Neither (generic QA structure)" in BOTH lanes: the shared context→answer map is tied neither to the assistant's helpful register (rude and evasive framings keep it) nor to speaking-to-a-user (addressee-free exposition and an AI-relay addressee keep it).

The parent round's finding is confirmed, not displaced: pure-GCV λ selection collapsed on judge-filtered row subsets. The refit repairs exactly the four collapsed kept fits (instruct helpful-instruction −1.481 → +0.662, instruct evasive −0.585 → +0.542, instruct AI-relay −1.205 → +0.656, base rude −0.002 → +0.144) while the six healthy fits move by at most 0.011 (four reproduce to four decimals), and the G1 anchor gate — kept at pure GCV by design so the reproduction target is meaningful — reproduces all four committed reference values (0.6542/0.6249 instruct, 0.5416/0.5783 base) to within 1.2e-16 (tolerance 0.01): **G1 PASSed both lanes**. The refit code path introduces no drift; the run-1 void was a selector artifact, full stop.

Secondary reads: instruct-lane maps are uniformly stronger than base (own-map R² 0.53–0.66 vs 0.13–0.40); all six instruction-matched secondary pairs also read Shared (weakest: base evasive vs helpful-instruction, 0.53, CI 0.52–0.55); the plan's re-anchoring rule never triggers; prefix-arm fits stay degenerate (R² −0.004 to 0.13) and carry no identity evidence.

### Evidence

- `eval_results/issue_1417/refit/battery_summary.json` at `3867276eea` (rel_l19, r2_l19, yields, verdicts, `h_table_lookup`, `refit_config`).
- Per-pair battery JSONs (`refit/battery/`, 28 pairs incl. prefix arms): `rel_bootstrap_l19` (1,000 draws), `composition_collapse_null_l19` + `procrustes_cosine_null_l19` (100 draws each), per-layer ceilings/numerators/cosines.
- Per-cell fits (`refit/cells/`, 160 files): `r2_per_layer_obs`, bootstrap CIs, `lambda_selection` provenance; run-1 counterparts under `eval_results/issue_1417/cells/` for the before/after contrast.
- `refit/anchors/g1_anchor_gate_{instruct,pretrained}.json`: `pass: true`, max `abs_dev` 1.1e-16.
- Figures committed to main at `2fef2c010f` (`refit_verdicts` hero + `refit_ceiling_vs_numerator` raw-components companion), per-point data in the `.meta.json` sidecars.

### Alternatives considered

1. **The Shared sweep is another instrument artifact (selector overfits toward the reference).** Rejected as the primary read: the inner-CV selector is chosen on inner conversation-grouped training splits of each fit's own rows with no access to the reference cell; the anchor gate reproduces committed values exactly; and the ceiling-independent reads (rotation-aligned cosine z ≈ 10²–10³ vs chance, frozen-map transfer positive both ways in run 1's healthy pair) agree with the ratio verdicts.
2. **Shared verdicts are inflated by attenuated ceilings (the ratio's denominator shrinks on weak cells).** Partially retained as a hedge: REL is a ratio, and base-lane ceilings (0.43–0.57 on kept∩kept rows) sit below full-n anchors, so 0.71–0.91 recovery is "map largely carried", not identity proof. This bounds the claim at MODERATE, not the verdict direction — the CI lattice grades Shared at every pair and the cosines corroborate.
3. **Content collapse in the rude cell manufactures its Shared read.** Contained: both rude cells sit below the 0.5 answer-variance floor (0.486 instruct, 0.462 base — the floor the plan set so a collapsed cell cannot carry a Distinct verdict), and base rude is additionally 10.9%-yield, n = 516. The helpful-register rejection therefore does not rest on rude alone: the evasive cell also violates helpful register and reads Shared (0.91 instruct / 0.73 base) with the base lane primary-grade (62% yield, variance ratio 0.78).
4. **The base rude Shared is noise at n = 516.** Scrutinized specifically (the brief's ask): own-map R² 0.144 clears its shuffle null by 0.19 (threshold 0.1); REL 0.71, CI 0.69–0.73 wholly above 0.5; composition null p97.5 −0.016 vs observed +0.302; aligned cosine 0.558 vs chance p97.5 0.00054. Internally consistent — but the bootstrap holds per-fold maps fixed (rows resampled), so the CI excludes map-refit variability, and the cell is doubly exploratory. Reported as the weakest Shared, hedged in body and Takeaways.
5. **Duplicate-question cross-fold leakage inflates all fits.** Carried over from run 1 as a line-wide caveat (largest cluster 32–35 identical rows); it affects cells and references symmetrically, so it inflates absolute R² more than the REL ratio.

### Confidence reasoning

MODERATE. For: 10/10 concordant verdicts across two model lanes with tight CIs; three independent read families agree (ratio lattice, cosines vs chance, run-1 healthy-pair transfers); exact anchor reproduction plus surgical repair (collapsed fits fixed, healthy fits untouched) pins the instrument story. Against HIGH: the one cell purpose-built to discriminate helpful register (rude) fails its content-variance floor in both lanes; four of ten cells sit below the 50% yield floor (base rude at 10.9%); a single generation seed per (cell, model); recovery fractions of 0.71–0.91 in the base lane are consistent with a largely-shared-but-attenuated map rather than strict identity; and whether the model actually registered the AI-relay framing is unverified (the acknowledgement rubric's production pass is unrun).
